thread_title: S. montana F1 Transylvania Co, NC
breadcrumb: S. montana F1 Transylvania Co, NC

posts.body_html:
here's a cross between two genetically different clones from the same population! I made this cross more than 10 years ago, kept the seeds in cold storage, and popped them maybe 5 or 6 years ago because most of the mother plants died out when I moved unfortunately. In any case, these are starting to look pretty nice this season: they were freshly transplanted and divided last winter, but appear as though they haven't skipped a beat! In a lot of cases, when you selectively breed plants, they're a bit more vigorous and grower friendly compared to the original wild types.

posts.body_html:
Those are truly beautiful. 
Having once lived in Transylvania Co, NC, even more so.
You have me dreaming of the mountains ! 

But I have a question - would a variety from Transylvania Co, NC, grow in my climate in the NW Florida Panhandle ?
We do get a cold snap, but not the length or as low temps as the mtns of NC
(wouldn't that be nice about now, it being 100 degrees !).

I'm thinking that to be healthy they would need a longer cold ? 
Or would they adapt ?? 

Thanks for any input, 
Patty
